hero.title: Questions first. Materials second.
hero.intro: I am interested in functional materials and devices where understanding the mechanism can make the next experiment more intentional.
hero.sideNote: My strongest base is experimental. I am expanding it with computational materials, DFT and machine learning so that prediction can join the workflow.

threads.title: How do structure and interfaces create useful behaviour?
threads.text: Interest in materials whose electrical, optical or interfacial properties can be translated into real device functions.

threads.title: Can devices become smaller, simpler and more self-sufficient?
threads.text: Curiosity around energy harvesting, sensing and systems that can operate closer to where the problem exists.

threads.title: What happens when materials thinking meets electronic systems?
threads.text: A growing interest in semiconductor materials, interfaces and the design constraints that shape practical devices.

computational.title: Computationally stronger, experimentally grounded.
computational.text: I am deliberately developing a second edge in DFT, Python and AI/ML. The goal is not to collect tools. It is to make future research more predictive and efficient.
computational.now: Building workflows that can eventually sit before the lab: screening, understanding trends, and deciding which experiments are worth doing.
computational.later: Projects will appear here when the method, question and result are strong enough to deserve their own research story.
